Definition: to gnaw, i.e. (figuratively) eat (by hyberbole); also (participle) a pain
BiblicalUsage: The word means to gnaw, and Job uses it for the misery that eats at him. The outcasts gnaw in the wilderness for want and famine, and in the night his bones are pierced, gnawed, and his sinews take no rest.
TheologicalSignificance: Suffering gnaws like a wild thing in the dark, and Job names it plainly instead of pretending it is not there.
